hero.subtitle: When a death in Sausalito was caused by someone else's carelessness, surviving family members may have a civil claim under California law. We connect you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who can explain it plainly.

about.title: Sausalito Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription:
Grief doesn't follow a schedule, but the law does. In California, most wrongful death claims must be filed within two years of the date a person died, and that window narrows sharply when a public agency is involved. That is hard to face while the loss is still raw.

Sausalito is a small waterfront community of roughly 7,156 people in Marin County, where daily life runs along Bridgeway and the US-101 corridor. Public records show 31 injury collisions and 38 people hurt in 2025, with no traffic deaths recorded that year. A wrongful death claim is not limited to the road, though. A fall at a rental property, a medical error, a defective product, or a boating incident on the bay can each give rise to one.

LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects surviving family members with an independent attorney who works on contingency. You describe what happened; the attorney explains who has standing, what may be recovered, and how the civil claim stands apart from any criminal case.

items.title: Clarity on who can file
items.desc: California limits who may bring a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. The attorney you're connected with will sort out standing before anything else.

items.title: The two-year deadline, explained
items.desc: Most claims must be filed within two years of the date of death, and the timeline is shorter when a city, county, or state agency is involved. Early guidance keeps those dates from slipping by.

items.title: No fee unless there's a recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network handle wrongful death cases on contingency, and our connection service is free. Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship, and guidance.

items.question: If a death in Sausalito involved a state highway like US-101 or a city vehicle, does the deadline change?
items.answer: It can. When a government entity such as Caltrans, Marin County, or the City of Sausalito may share responsibility, California generally requires a formal claim to be presented far sooner than the usual two years. Missing that earlier step can close the door on the case, so it's worth speaking with an attorney quickly to confirm which deadline applies.

items.question: Is a wrongful death lawsuit the same as criminal charges?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action brought by family members to recover losses, while a criminal case is brought by the district attorney to punish conduct. The two proceed separately, and a civil claim can go forward whether or not charges are ever filed.

items.question: My sibling died. Can I bring the claim?
items.answer: Standing in California is layered. A surviving spouse or domestic partner and children come first; if none exist, certain dependents or heirs may be able to file. An attorney can review your family's situation and tell you honestly whether you qualify.
